_meta.source: Export restrictions on record, IFPRI Food and Fertilizer Export Restrictions Tracker pattern; every entry re-verified on 2026-09-16 against the primary notification or a wire report, cited per row
_meta.notes: Statuses: official (a government notification in force), reported (a measure reported in force by a wire source), historical (lifted or window closed, kept on record). Exposure (who is hit) is computed live from the atlas by restrictionExposure() and is real regardless of status. No entry without a source_url. The IFPRI tracker itself has no downloadable table (checked 2026-09-16: Shiny app and API only), so verification runs against primary sources. Next review due after 30 days. 2026-09-24: Malawi maize export ban (in force, Ministry of Trade 2 Jun 2026) and Zambia's April 2026 lifting added after checking the primary reports.

data.source_name: DGFT notification of 13 May 2026, reported by Business Standard, 14 May 2026
data.note: Sugar export policy moved from restricted to prohibited with immediate effect through 30 September 2026, on domestic stock concerns. EU and US tariff-rate quota shipments, advance-authorisation and pipeline cargoes are exempt. In force on 24 September 2026; no extension announced by then (checked against DGFT notices and wire reports; the 'India to extend sugar export ban' reports that surface are from September 2024). If not extended, sugar exports revert from 'prohibited' to 'restricted' on 1 October 2026.

next_step.text: export policy reverts to restricted (quota) unless the ban is extended
next_step.source_name: DGFT notification of 13 May 2026 (prohibited till 30 September 2026)

data.source_name: Trade Ministry regulation Permendag 16/2026, reported by Antara, 9 Jun 2026
data.note: Permendag 16/2026 sets a transition from 1 June to 31 December 2026 for palm oil derivative exports under export permits. From 1 January 2027 only designated state-owned exporters holding a valid export permit may ship. A permit regime, not a ban.

next_step.text: only designated state-owned exporters with a valid export permit may ship palm oil derivatives

data.source_name: DGFT Notification 20/2023-24; lifting reported by IFPRI, 2024
data.note: Ban on non-basmati white rice exports from 20 July 2023. Lifted 28 September 2024 for a 490 dollar per tonne minimum export price, itself removed 20 October 2024. India's 2025 rice exports reached about 21.5 Mt with the curbs gone. Nothing comparable in force on 16 September 2026.
Outright ban on palm oil and cooking oil exports from 28 April 2022, revoked from 23 May 2022 by Regulation 30/2022. The export-permit regime now in force is the separate official entry above.

data.source_name: Government of Russia decree (2026 quota); earlier years via Interfax
data.note: Tariff-rate export quota each 15 February to 30 June since 2021: 24 to 29 Mt in 2024, 11 Mt in 2025, 20 Mt in 2026. The 2026 window closed on 30 June. From 1 September 2026 the wheat, barley and corn export duty is set to zero through year end (Bloomberg, 2 September 2026), an easing, not a restriction.

Exports restricted beyond 31 October 2023 for an indefinite period on lower cane output; 1 Mt allowed for 2024-25 and 1.5 Mt for 2025-26. Superseded by the outright prohibition of 13 May 2026, the official entry above.

data.source_name: Malawi Ministry of Trade spokesperson, reported by Times 360 Malawi, 2 Jun 2026
data.note: Maize export ban imposed in November 2025; the Ministry of Trade said on 2 June 2026 that it remains in force and that exports are illegal. No end date announced. Latest confirmation found on the review date, 24 September 2026, is the June statement.

data.source_name: Zambia Ministry of Agriculture statement, reported by News Diggers, 9 Apr 2026
data.note: Zambia removed its restrictions on exporting maize grain and maize products, including mealie meal, on 9 April 2026, after the 2024 El Niño-drought ban; government cited strategic reserves of about 700,000 t. A new ban in a 2027 drought would be the measure to watch.
